newsitem.title: PERU: Red Cross man calls late on besieged Peru house.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross man calls late on besieged Peru house.

text.p: A Red Cross official walked into the besieged Japanese ambassador's house in Lima early Saturday and was still inside over half an hour later, witnesses said.
The man, wearing the white vest of the Red Cross, was seen by reporters as he strolled into the residence, where Marxist rebels are holding 72 hostages, just before 2 a.m. local time.
There was no explanation for the visit at such an unusual hour, and an official at the Red Cross office in Lima gave no information. Reports varied as to whether the man was carrying anything.
In the past, visits by Red Cross doctors to the residence have led to speculation about ill health among the hostages or the roughly 20 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels holding them.

None of the hostages have been reported acutely ill recently. But a few suffer from diabetes, heart disease or other chronic illnesses, and several are reported to be suffering from stress-related disorders.
